HO00007292.title: DocHouse: Among Mountains and Streams
HO00007292.description:
In a mysterious forest, far from the borders of the China they’ve left behind, the painter Meng Huang and writer Ma Jian talk about exile, political opposition and artistic creation as a response to oppression and lies.
The dissident writer, who has been unable to return to China, where all of his books are banned, since 2011, and the renowned painter living in exile in Berlin, are haunted by memories of the country they have fled. As leaves fall around them, they journey through the forest contemplating persecution, resistance and the role of their work. For the two artists, whose world view has been upended by the Tiananmen Square massacre, creation offers an answer.

HO00007355.title: DocHouse: Black is Beautiful
HO00007355.description:
Photographer, freedom fighter and activist Kwame Brathwaite took 500,000 photos across his 60-year career, always devoted to celebrating the joy and beauty of African American life. Everyone knows the phrase 'Black is Beautiful', but few know about the man who helped popularise it. 

Starting in Harlem in the 1950’s, Kwame Brathwaite took half a million photos including many of 'regular' people on the street but also thousands of intimate and unexpected photos of stars including Stevie Wonder, Muhammad Ali, Marvin Gaye, Roberta Flack, Nina Simone, and the Jackson Five.

At a time when this was deemed radical, Kwame’s photos of Black communities and people focused on beauty and joy instead of trauma and conflict. Kwame also pioneered grassroots fashion shows that celebrated natural Black beauty, heralding a new dawn across the globe.

BLACK IS BEAUTIFUL tells Kwame's life story, celebrating his arresting photography, and finally giving the man called “the soul” of the Black is Beautiful movement his shine.

HO00007352.title: DocHouse: Boorman and the Devil
HO00007352.description: BOORMAN AND THE DEVIL details how Academy Award-nominated director John Boorman took on the massive 1977 sequel Exorcist II: The Heretic, turning down standard horror tropes for a high-budget, metaphysical misfire that became one of Hollywood's most famous box-office disasters.

HO00007336.title: DocHouse: Celtic Utopia
HO00007336.description:
After 100 years of independence, a bold new wave of young Irish artists redefine folk music and reflect on the impact of their colonial history.

The Irish folk music renaissance sees artists coming from punk, hip-hop, and beyond, rediscovering an ancient tradition and taking it in unexpected directions. 

In CELTIC UTOPIA, artists including The Mary Wallopers, The Deadlians, Poor Creature, Negro Impacto and Lankum take us on a ballad tour around the island, telling stories and singing songs to try to understand their past and to heal their colonial wounds. Archive footage ties the present moment to Ireland’s troubled past, and creates a rich portrait of an island coming to terms with a century of independence.

HO00007356.title: DocHouse: Christine Choy: Double Bill
HO00007356.description:
The first programme in our retrospective of pioneering Asian American filmmaker Christine Choy is a double bill of two short films reflecting Choy's interest in the little-shown experience of East and Southeast Asian immigrants to the US. Giving voice to workers, community leaders and refugees, the films were unusual for their focus and candour at the time, and are still strikingly humanistic testaments to the complexity of the immigrant experience.

Featuring FROM SPIKES TO SPINDLES (1976, 45 mins) and BITTERSWEET SURVIVAL: SOUTHEAST ASIAN REFUGEES IN AMERICA (1982, 30 mins)

HO00007343.title: DocHouse: Don't Look Back in Anger
HO00007343.description: DON'T LOOK BACK IN ANGER charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s triumphant reunion tour, Oasis Live ‘25, one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time. The film is an unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world. The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years. Alongside the band’s sold-out world tour, the film also explores the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what their music means to audiences and generations worldwide.

HO00007323.title: DocHouse: How Deep is Your Love
HO00007323.description:
With mesmerising underwater cinematography, HOW DEEP IS YOUR LOVE takes us way down below the surface with a team of scientists exploring the unknown: the deep sea, where 70% of our planet lies hidden.

Their life's work is finding, describing and naming strange and wonderful deep sea creatures, and now they find themselves racing against the looming threat of deep-sea mining, as they search for thriving ecosystems in the unexplored darkness.

Director Eleanor Mortimer weaves wonder with urgency, challenging us to balance the drive for resources with the intrinsic value of an ecosystem. As we journey through this breathtaking realm, we are left to ponder – how deep is our love?

HO00007342.title: DocHouse: In-I in Motion
HO00007342.description:
In 2007, French actress Juliette Binoche and British dancer-choreographer Akram Khan stepped away from their established careers to embark on a bold artistic experiment. Over six months, they co-created In-I, an intense, boundary-pushing performance they would go on to stage 100 times around the world.
Today, Juliette Binoche returns to that intimate journey. From the first spark of inspiration to the final applause, she retraces the emotional and creative arc of a singular collaboration. Drawing on dozens of hours of previously unseen footage, she reflects, as a filmmaker, on the nature of artistic creation, the vulnerability and exhilaration of taking risks, and the personal transformation they demand.

HO00007346.title: DocHouse: Kikuyu Land
HO00007346.description:
While investigating Kenya's global tea industry, Nairobi journalist Bea Wangondu stumbles upon her own family's concealed secrets, pushing her to peel back the layers of Kenya's colonial legacy.

When the British colonised Kenya, they took control of prime tea-growing land, stripping Kikuyu people of Central Kenya of their lands and cultural identity. The plantations are still owned by some of the world's biggest corporations, supplying the global market, with local Kenyan's left to labour under abusive conditions on their own ancestral soil. 

As Bea follows a local man's legal challenge to retrieve his family's stolen land, she discovers a murky world of hidden evidence and untold wounds. Set against the beautifully captured richness of the landscape, KIKUYU LAND is a poetic, stunningly cinematic dive into a complex history.

HO00007357.title: DocHouse: Mississippi Triangle
HO00007357.description:
The second part of our retrospective of pioneering Asian American filmmaker Christine Choy is the newly-restored 1984 feature MISSISSIPPI TRIANGLE, an intimate portrait of the Mississippi Delta, where Chinese, African American and white locals live in a complex world of cotton, labour and racial conflict.

The history of the Chinese community, originally brought to the South to work on cotton plantations after the Civil War, is framed against the harsh realities of civil rights, religion, politics, and class in the South. Rare historical footage and interviews of Delta residents are combined to create this unprecedented document of inter-ethnic relations in the American South.

HO00007341.title: DocHouse: Remake
HO00007341.description: In REMAKE, filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, SHERMAN’S MARCH. What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

HO00007339.title: DocHouse: Sherman's March
HO00007339.description:
Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman’s 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South.
A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, SHERMAN’S MARCH is a landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV. Now restored in beautiful 4k.

HO00007294.title: DocHouse: Shorts: Maybe Tomorrow + Allies in Exile
HO00007294.description:
This double bill of short films from exceptional Syrian filmmakers brings together stories of the bonds of friendship, displacement, loss and endurance during Assad's regime and in the precarious time since its sudden end.

MAYBE TOMORROW, directed by Wafa Mustafa and Waad Al-Kateab (FOR SAMA) follows Wafa's long search for her father, who was disappeared under Assad's regime. In ALLIES IN EXILE, filmmakers and friends Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al Halabi turn from documenting the frontlines of a revolution to filming the bureaucracy of exile whilst housed in a UK asylum hotel.

HO00007291.title: DocHouse: Super Nature
HO00007291.description:
A love letter to nature filmed exclusively on Super 8 (the original and beloved home movie format), SUPER NATURE invites us on a cinematic and richly rewarding global tour of connection with the natural world. 
To capture the whole world on camera, director Ed Sayers collaborated with 40 people filming the nature closest to their homes and their hearts on 80 different Super 8 cameras - across the land, in the air and under water. 

A celebration of all we have and a reflection on all we have to lose, this global co-creation project journeys across 25 different countries, creating a visceral, poetic and personal meditation on the world we live in.

HO00007347.title: DocHouse: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
HO00007347.description:
KNIFE explores renowned author Salman Rushdie’s life, career and recovery following a harrowing attempt on his life in 2022. The film includes never-before-seen footage shot by Rushdie’s wife, the American poet, novelist and visual artist Rachel Eliza Griffiths, in the time following the attack offering a graphic, unflinching, and deeply intimate account of his remarkable recovery and optimism for the future. Directed by Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney, KNIFE is inspired by Rushdie’s bestselling memoir ‘Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder.’
Special preview screenings on 30 September with theatrically exclusive recorded Q&A with Alex Gibney, Salman Rushdie and Rachel Eliza Griffiths

HO00007322.title: DocHouse: The Cycle Of Love
HO00007322.description:
In 1977, PK, a young street artist from Delhi, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile journey to find the woman who had captured his heart.

Growing up poor and 'untouchable', young PK had to reckon with the caste system and with his own sense of self-worth, as he met fellow travellers and locals from all walks of life on his journey across the world. Oscar-nominated director Orlando von Einsiedel retraces PK's journey from India to Sweden in an extraordinarily uplifting film, that is not just about what can happen when you follow your heart, but is also a paean to the joy of chance encounters and the kindness of strangers.

HO00007358.title: DocHouse: The Disciple
HO00007358.description:
An outsider fueled by relentless determination works his way into the inner circle of the Wu-Tang Clan, where his ambition and creativity converge in the making of an album poised to ignite global controversy.

Wu-Tang Clan’s seventh studio album, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin, was recorded in secret over six years, sealed in an ornate silver case, and first sold at a 2015 auction for a reported $2 million, under terms barring any commercial release until 2103. 

In THE DISCIPLE, director Joanna Natasegara tells the story of the album's unlikely origins and controversial reception, meeting Tarik Azzougharh - the Dutch-Moroccan superfan who talked his way into Wu-Tang Clan's inner circle and became the driving force of the now legendary album, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin.

HO00007293.title: DocHouse: The Gardener, The Buddhist and the Spy
HO00007293.description:
A corporate spy in the pocket of the asbestos industry, or a whistleblower uncovering corruption? When Rob Moore invites two journalists to tell his story, the lines between intentions and consequences begin to blur.
For five years, former TV producer Rob poses as a filmmaker to gain the trust of anti-asbestos activists, whilst being paid to spy on them by the asbestos industry. When he is exposed as a cynical fraud, he claims to be a double agent, working alone to feed  false information to the international asbestos mafia.

In a bid to launder his reputation and regain credibility, Rob lets two journalists begin work on a podcast about him, but as they delve deeper into the shady case, inconsistencies and ethical dilemmas cast doubt on Rob's version of events.  One twist leads to another in a gripping film about the delicate balance between good, evil, influence and control.

HO00007359.title: DocHouse: The Last First: Winter K2
HO00007359.description:
Director Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that takes an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture.

Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory.

THE LAST FIRST: WINTER K2 takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story - one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power - all under life-and-death circumstances.

HO00007338.title: DocHouse: The Watergate Caper
HO00007338.description:
This archival documentary traces the rise and fall of Nixon from the presidential primaries of 1968 through the Watergate break-in of June 1972 to his resignation two years later, killing trust in the political process and the American presidency in the wake of the Vietnam War.
 The film draws on hundreds of hours of TV news taped off-air by the Nixon White House to tell the untold story of the Watergate burglars. How did tapping the wrong phone with a bug that didn't work lead to their arrests and Nixon's resignation? It also explores representations of the Nixon years in popular culture, using the music, commercials, and cinema of the era to evoke a fevered political landscape of culture wars, dirty tricks, paranoia and assassination. Sound familiar?

HO00007266.title: DocHouse: What We Were and What We Are
HO00007266.description:
First-time directors from the Sahrawi Refugee camps explore how their culture has changed after 50 years of enforced displacement. World Premiere screening of films and a Q&A. Organised by IRSAAN, UCL and UAL

WHAT WE WERE AND WHAT WE ARE is an event centered on a World Premiere screening of documentary films made by first-time directors from the Sahrawi Refugee camps. The young filmmakers have made works about their elders and how the Sahrawi culture has changed after 50 years of enforced displacement. The event will also comprise of talks and opportunities for Q&A sessions with the filmmakers and members of IRSAAN a Sahrawi led health charity based in the camps.

HO00007335.title: DocHouse: Yuja
HO00007335.description: Daredevil. Rebel. Powerhouse. At 39, Yuja Wang stands among the most electrifying musicians of our time and she is falling out of love with the music. In YUJA, acclaimed filmmaker Lorna Tucker crafts an immersive portrait of an artist in flux. With unprecedented access, the film weaves together performance, memory, and reconstruction to explore the forces that shape Yuja, and the woman she is still becoming.

HO00007351.title: DocHouse:All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea
HO00007351.description:
When thousands of dead crabs wash ashore in aa small North East fishing town, fisherman Stan Rennie becomes the unlikeliest of activists, in a grassroots fight for answers and a future.

Stan has worked this stretch of coastline, where the river meets the sea, for over fifty years. So when a vast tide of poisoned crabs, lobster and shellfish washes onto the beach, and officials seem unable or unwilling to establish a cause,  Stan finds himself thrown into battle: the unlikely figurehead of the campaign to uncover the truth about the die-off. 

Directed by Teessider Jeanie Finlay, this is a wry, David and Goliath story about navigating through grief and finding power in community, rich with Stan's own brand of heart, determination and gallows humour.

HO00007340.title: The Final Film Festival: Plane Film + Q&A
HO00007340.description:
In an effort to continue using filmmaking as exposure therapy (after conquering her fear of the Tube in Tube Film), filmmaker Orla Smith tackles an even bigger fear: planes. On a trip to Porto, the camera is wielded as a shield against panic attacks. But this time, things don’t go exactly to plan.

I worried that without a film to work, on I wasn’t happy”, reads a text box at the start of Plane Film, a personal documentary / anxiety spiral by filmmaker Orla Smith. This encore screening follows the film’s competition win at The Final Film Festival (it won the recently christened Final d’Or), and it fits well with the festival’s name, as Plane Film is a film that restlessly wonders whether cinema is helping or hurting us.

Confronting air travel also forces Orla to confront something else: her compulsive need to document herself through her films as a form of self-administered therapy — or is it avoidance? A camera has helped her overcome some of her biggest fears, but it has also been a way to put distance between herself and the people around her. Plane Film is a film at war with itself, and with the concept of filmmaking in general. Should we throw the whole thing away? Should this be the final film festival after all? 

- Orla Smith

HO00007344.title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
HO00007344.description:
KNIFE explores renowned author Salman Rushdie’s life, career and recovery following a harrowing attempt on his life in 2022. The film includes never-before-seen footage shot by Rushdie’s wife, the American poet, novelist and visual artist Rachel Eliza Griffiths, in the time following the attack offering a graphic, unflinching, and deeply intimate account of his remarkable recovery and optimism for the future.

Directed by Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney, KNIFE is inspired by Rushdie’s bestselling memoir ‘Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder.’

Q&A in partnership with The Nerve

Bag searches will take place on entry to the screening on Saturday 12 September at Mayfair.

HO00007327.title: Ukrainian Film Fest: Decay
HO00007327.description:
The first fiction feature made about the Chornobyl disaster. On the eve of the accident the journalist Oleksandr Zhuravlov returns to Kyiv, to his family and to the friends of his childhood. The next day the ordinary course of events changes for good. The state conceals the true scale of what has happened; Zhuravlov refuses to accept the official account and sets out to establish the truth. Two further strands run alongside his: the newlyweds Valerii and Liuba, who slip away from their own wedding and end up inside the contaminated zone, and a boy who is left behind in Prypiat with his cat, because the cat could not be taken out.
Introduced by the film scholar and archivist, Stanislav Menzelevskyi, in person.
Presented in partnership with the Centre for Eurasian, Russian and East European Studies (CEREES) at Queen Mary University of London.
The screening follows the symposium ‘Visualising Chornobyl: Ukraine and Beyond’, marking the fortieth anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster, which takes place on 18 September at Queen Mary University of London. The symposium is organised by CEREES at Queen Mary University of London and the British Association for Slavonic & East European Studies (BASEES).

Programme supported by Film Hub London, managed by Film London. Proud to be a partner of the BFI Film Audience Network, funded by the National Lottery.

HO00007331.title: Ukrainian Film Fest: U Are the Universe
HO00007331.description:
The near future. Andriy Melnyk, a Ukrainian space trucker, hauls nuclear waste aboard a cargo ship to Callisto, an abandoned moon of Jupiter. During an otherwise routine flight the Earth explodes, and Andriy survives. He is left believing himself to be the last person in the universe — until Catherine, a French woman on a faraway space station, makes contact with him. Andriy decides to go and see her, despite every obstacle.

HO00007330.title: Ukrainian Film Fest: Shorts by Female Directors
HO00007330.description:
This program brings together six short films by Ukrainian female directors that centre female experience within the shifting realities of present-day Ukraine. Working across fiction and animation, the filmmakers approach questions of identity, intimacy, displacement, and self-determination with precision and emotional clarity.

Taken together, these films do not present a single narrative of womanhood. Instead, they offer a range of perspectives shaped by different ages, contexts, and artistic approaches. What unites them is a commitment to placing women’s voices at the centre — attentive to everyday experience while remaining conscious of the broader political and social conditions in which these lives unfold.

Curated by Sasha Prokopenko and Olga Gusiatynska, in partnership with Kyiv International Short Film Festival
Kittens, dir. Zhanna Ozirna, 2023, 9`

Two girls in a Lviv apartment begin a normal conversation about their future together. Amidst the remnants of traditional Ukrainian life, ordinary dreams of tomorrow come up against fossilised social norms and orders. Some people have to fight society for things that most people take for granted. Surrounded by everyday scenery and dealing with the usual household tasks, their sincere conversation turns into a global question.

The Diaper Cake, dir. Anastasia Babenko, 2021, 18`

Lena and Vitya, both in their early twenties, are two kids who now have a kid of their own. In the postnatal hospital room, as if suspended in limbo, their first team project is to wake their son for a feeding. As the new parents are trying to do their best, they have to deal with the irreversible changes in their lives and with each other. Meanwhile, the diaper cake silently sits in the room, like a time bomb.

Kira, dir. Anastasiia Obodovska, 2023, 27`

When the full-scale invasion begins, Kira can’t get away from her internal fever — she has to go to the frontline. She is 28 and she is a veterinarian, so it is natural for her to become a paramedic. But there is one ‘but’ — her twelve-year-old son, Vitia, whom Kira is raising alone. So the first question is: with whom to leave the child? The second question is whether Kira can really leave her son. She has been a mother most of her life. She has always protected her son herself, always been there for him. Maybe it’s time to protect something else?

The Seventh Shift, dir. Natalia Ilchuk, 2023, 15`

‘The Seventh Shift’ is a portrait of a solitary woman who works four jobs in a nearly abandoned Ukrainian town. She manages to maintain her integrity by avoiding the paradigms imposed by the social conditions of existence, focusing instead on the world beyond the material dimension with its many limitations. Continual ritual gestures that do not involve obtaining a profit, and an irrational faith in an unattainable future, have become the main basis of this film where prosaic reality is not expressed explicitly but through the visual poetry of an industrial town in decay.

I Died in Irpin, dir. Anastasiia Falilieieva, 2024, 11`

On the 24th of February in the morning, my boyfriend and I decided to go from Kyiv to Irpin to see his parents. It is hard for me to recall the chronology of those days, my mind blocks and minimises all the memories, erases them, but the only thing I know for sure is that every day everything rapidly became worse.

Prelude, dir. Alina Panasenko, 2025, 14`

While cruising through the nocturnal streets of war-shadowed Kyiv, Anna — a civilian woman with a camera — films passing men with quiet intensity. Her lens lingers on their faces, bodies, and movements, capturing fragments of masculinity. One night, she unexpectedly encounters a soldier — not just another subject, but someone who interrupts the frame. Their conversation begins awkwardly, circling around the men she’s observed, but unfolds into a strange but deep connection.

Followed by an online Q&A with the directors.

HO00007328.title: Ukrainian Film Fest: The Last Prometheus of Donbas
HO00007328.description:
A few kilometres from the front line stands the thermal power plant in Kurakhove — the last operational power station in the free part of the Donetsk region. At a moment when Russia is trying to deprive the country of light and heat, the workers of the plant risk their lives every day, because every time the station is brought back on line it becomes a target. The film follows their daily struggle for light and heat, shows the workings of this industrial giant of the Donetsk region, and pays tribute to the people who kept it running. Archival footage from the 1930s, when the plant was built, is set against the present. Evacuation, in the end, proves unavoidable.

Followed by a Q&A with the director Anton Shtuka in person.

Programme supported by Film Hub London, managed by Film London. Proud to be a partner of the BFI Film Audience Network, funded by the National Lottery.

HO00007329.title: Ukrainian Film Fest: Militantropos
HO00007329.description:
Militantropos captures the human condition through the fractured realities of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The film assembles everyday lives transformed by war — those who flee, those who lose everything, and those who stay behind to resist and to fight — following both the instinct to survive and the need for closeness. The title joins the Latin ‘milit’ (soldier) with the Greek ‘anthropos’ (human), and names the figure a person becomes once war has absorbed them.

Followed by a Q&A with the co-director Simon Mozghovy in person.

Programme supported by Film Hub London, managed by Film London. Proud to be a partner of the BFI Film Audience Network, funded by the National Lottery.
